title: OpenCV Quiz
description: Revisit the key ideas in OpenCV. Read each choice carefully. You can try the quiz again after reviewing the lessons.

questions.question: Which number gives the width here?
questions.explanation: OpenCV is a library for working with images. A small colour image can be stored as rows, columns and three colour values per pixel. The output is (3, 4, 3). There are three rows, four columns and three colour channels. zeros makes a black image with every value equal to zero.

questions.question: What colour is this BGR pixel?
questions.explanation: OpenCV commonly uses blue, green, red order for colour images. Each uint8 channel can hold a whole number from 0 to 255. The output is [255, 0, 0]. In OpenCV BGR order, this pixel is blue because the first channel is at its maximum.

questions.question: What does BGR2RGB change?
questions.explanation: A colour conversion can reorder channels so another tool reads them correctly. COLOR_BGR2RGB swaps the blue and red positions. The output is [0, 0, 255]. It is still the same blue colour, now described in RGB order.

questions.question: How many channel values per pixel are in gray?
questions.explanation: Grayscale stores one brightness value per pixel. It drops colour detail while keeping a brightness view useful for some image operations. The output is (2, 3) 100. Equal BGR values of 100 become a gray value of 100. The result has no three-channel dimension.

questions.question: Is row 3 included in the slice 1:3?
questions.explanation: Cropping selects a rectangle from an image. NumPy slices use start positions and stop just before the end positions. The output is [[7, 8, 9], [12, 13, 14]]. Rows 1 and 2 and columns 2, 3 and 4 are selected. copy makes a separate array.

questions.question: What order does resize use for its size tuple?
questions.explanation: Resizing changes image dimensions. OpenCV resize takes the target size as width, height, unlike the row-first array shape. The output is (2, 3, 3). The requested width is 3 and height is 2. Nearest-neighbour resizing selects nearby pixel values.

questions.question: What happens to the value exactly 100 here?
questions.explanation: Thresholding turns brightness values into two groups. A binary threshold sets values above the limit to a maximum and the rest to zero. The output is [[0, 0, 255]]. Only 150 is greater than 100. A value equal to the threshold stays zero for this mode.

questions.question: What does the kernel size describe?
questions.explanation: Blurring combines neighbouring pixel values to soften local changes. A kernel is the small neighbourhood used for the calculation. The output is True True. Some brightness spreads from the centre to nearby pixels, so the centre becomes dimmer and its neighbour becomes brighter.

questions.question: Does Canny label the object as a square?
questions.explanation: An edge is a strong image change, often in brightness. Canny finds candidate edges after several processing steps; an edge is not an object label. The output is (20, 20) True. The result keeps the image size and contains nonzero edge pixels around the bright square. It does not name the shape for us.

questions.question: Which point coordinate names the column?
questions.explanation: OpenCV drawing points use x, y order. x is the column and y is the row. A negative thickness can fill a shape. The centre pixel is [0, 255, 0], which is green in BGR. The corner pixel remains [0, 0, 0]. The rectangle fills the selected area.

questions.question: Which value is kept at the bottom right?
questions.explanation: A mask is an image that marks which pixels to include. In this operation, a nonzero mask value allows the source pixel through. The output is [[10, 0], [0, 40]]. The mask keeps the two diagonal pixels and blocks the other two.

questions.question: What should you check after imwrite?
options: Its success result and the saved file
questions.explanation: imwrite saves image pixels to a file. Check its return value and choose a practice path so you do not overwrite work you need. On a writable practice folder with PNG support, the output is True and a small green PNG file is saved. False or an error means the save did not succeed.
